messages:
pagerduty_bot: [URGENT] PagerDuty alert: service=redwood-api-ingress severity=high — TLS handshake failures spike across us-east-1. Triggering incident channel.

devops_oncall: I'm on it. paging @network_ops @sarah_engineer. Initial graph shows TLS handshake error rate up ~320% at 06:12UTC. customer impact: some 5xxs and client-side timeouts.

support_lead: multiple customers reporting failures for inference requests. Ticket count rising. Not all regions affected, primarily us-east-1 frontends.

network_ops: I'm seeing logs from ingress LB: repeated "TLSv1.2 alert handshake_failure" and "no shared cipher" in the NLB logs. Also sporadic TCP RSTs. Pulling ELB access logs now.

sarah_engineer: grabbing app-side logs and envs. Not seeing internal cert rotation job running in the last 24h — it ran fine yesterday. Checking secret-manager rotation events.

alice_reliability: thanks. can someone run a quick openssl against the failing edge IPs? I want to know if it's server side or client negotiation.

network_ops: running: 

```
openssl s_client -connect ingress-us-east-1-1.redwood.internal:443 -servername api.redwood.com -msg -state
```

Output: 

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 307 bytes
---
3010:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure:ssl/s23_clnt.c:770:
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

network_ops: server seems to immediately send an alert. That suggests server rejected the cipher/client offer or server failed while selecting cert.

devops_oncall: timeline so far: 06:08UTC small uptick; 06:12UTC spike, incidents page. Any recent deploys? eng-releases: were there infra changes?

alice_reliability: devops deploys show no app image pushes at that time. There was a maintenance job touching the private CA rotation in KMS around 06:00UTC (runbook: rotate-intermediate-cert). @security any scheduled rotation?

security: yes, we kicked off automated intermediate cert rotation to test new HSM key binding at 05:58UTC. I see successful creation records but rotation didn't mark complete in vault — investigating.

sarah_engineer: if cert rotation left LB without a valid cert chain, TLS handshakes would fail. But why only some frontends? Could be VPC peering/nat path differences or cached listeners.

network_ops: cross-checking VPC peering and route tables: noticing packet drops at one of the transit gateways between us-east-1-a subnet and edge fleet. Also several ICMP fragmentation-needed logs — possible MTU mismatch after a route change.

devops_oncall: ok hypothesis A: incomplete cert rotation left some edge nodes with no valid cert -> handshake failures. Hypothesis B: MTU / fragmentation causing TLS handshake packets (ClientHello size ~1.8k with SNI+alpn) to be dropped -> handshake terminates.

alice_reliability: collecting evidence buckets. Evidence for A: rotation job started 05:58UTC and there are vault logs showing a partial write and then a timeout at 06:04UTC. Evidence for B: tcpdump from host-egress shows ICMP type3 code4 (fragmentation needed) to a subset of client IP ranges at 06:10-06:14UTC.

network_ops: pasting tcpdump excerpt:

```
06:10:12.123456 IP 10.0.1.45 > 10.1.2.200: ICMP 3/4, mtu 1400, length 556
06:10:12.123459 IP 10.0.1.46.443 > 10.1.2.200.52345: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```

network_ops: MTU on transit gw is 1500, but one peering route was created with an MTU of 1400 during the rotation of the transit appliance. That could mismatch.

sarah_engineer: quick replicate: from a failing client we see TLS ClientHello sent in 3 TCP segments due to MSS lowering, server never responds. When I forced path MTU discovery disabled, some handshakes succeed. That's consistent with fragmentation interfering with TLS ClientHello (larger than path MTU when using certain ciphers/extensions).

devops_oncall: customer impact assessment: roughly 18% of p95 latency requests turned into immediate failures for customers behind the affected transit path. Most other customers degraded with increased retries.

support_lead: adding impacted customers list to incident tracker and emailing affected accounts now with ETA unknown.

alice_reliability: running a hotfix plan: rollback the transit route change to restore MTU to 1500 and re-run cert rotation in a controlled manner. Who can apply rollback?

network_ops: I can push rollback to peering route within 2 minutes. Will do: `aws ec2 replace-transit-gateway-route --transit-gateway-route-table-id tgw-rtb-xyz --destination-cidr-block <edge-subnet> --transit-gateway-attachment-id tgw-attach-abc`

devops_oncall: proceed. notify when done.

network_ops: rollback applied at 06:20UTC. Monitoring.

pagerduty_bot: Incident status updated: mitigation in progress by network_ops. Severity: high -> mitigation.

sarah_engineer: re-testing openssl against same host — now handshake proceeds to server cert

```
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.3
    Cipher    : TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
```

sarah_engineer: logs show cert chain presented, good.

devops_oncall: metrics: handshake failures dropping back to baseline by 06:23UTC. RTT and p95 latency returning to normal by 06:25UTC.

support_lead: started post-update customer messages: 6 accounts affected initially, updates sent that we mitigated and investigating root cause. CS is on standby for followups.

alice_reliability: next steps for RCA: 1) capture full vault rotation logs and HSM responses around 05:58–06:05UTC, 2) audit transit gateway change events and who/what created MTU-lowered peering at 05:59–06:06UTC, 3) examine LB listener config to ensure certs deployed to all nodes, 4) produce timeline doc.

security: note — if rotation wrote partial chain to some nodes and then route change caused fragmentation, the combination explains skewed geography of failures. We'll need to validate whether any cert material was truncated during KV write timeouts.

network_ops: saving tcpdump, traceroute, and route-table snapshots to /incidents/1815552468/pcap and /incidents/1815552468/route-snapshots (internal path).

devops_oncall: assigning owners: vault logs -> security; rotation replay & cert deployment -> alice_reliability; transit route audit & rollback analysis -> network_ops; customer comms -> support_lead. We'll prepare a draft incident timeline and post here.

alice_reliability: quick timeline draft:
- 05:58UTC: automated intermediate cert rotation job triggered
- 05:59–06:04UTC: partial write to vault; timeout observed
- 05:59–06:06UTC: transit-gateway peering route created with MTU 1400 by an infra automation job
- 06:08UTC: small uptick in handshake failures
- 06:12UTC: spike in TLS handshake errors; PagerDuty alerts fired
- 06:20UTC: network_ops rolled back peering change to MTU 1500
- 06:23UTC: failures drop to baseline

devops_oncall: labeling hypotheses in-thread:
- H1: Cert rotation incomplete -> nodes had invalid/missing chain -> direct handshake failure. (evidence: vault partial write, initial server alert)
- H2: MTU mismatch -> fragmentation prevented full ClientHello -> handshake can't complete on affected path. (evidence: ICMP frag-needed, success after MTU rollback)
- H3: Combination -> some nodes with missing cert + MTU issues amplified failure surface. (evidence: mixed geography and partial recoveries)

network_ops: what logs do we need to close H2? I have pcaps showing ICMP3/4 but need per-flow retrans and router MTU settings. I'll export flows and attach.

security: we'll pull KMS/HSM audit logs and vault write traces. Also will check if rotation job triggered any load on the key master that could cause timeouts.

support_lead: CS asking for a root-cause statement for customers — we'll wait until we have consensus. Will continue to send status updates every 2 hours.

devops_oncall: post-incident action items assigned. Plan to schedule a follow-up war-room for RCA tomorrow at 14:00UTC. Closing incident channel once the RCA doc is posted.

alice_reliability: immediate mitigation checklist for runbook update: 1) ensure transit peering automations don't change MTU without approval; 2) make cert rotation idempotent and verify full chain propagation before deprecating old cert; 3) add path-MTU safety check as part of rotation testing.

network_ops: attaching final logs and PCAP pointers in the incident tracker. I'll also open a playbook PR to block MTU changes during cert operations.

devops_oncall: thanks all. incident moving to post-mortem stage. If anything else pops up, reply here.

support_lead: noted. I'll follow up with all impacted customers once RCA is finalized. :white_check_mark:
